Isoniazid is considered to be unsafe in patients with porphyria although there is conflicting experimental evidence of porphyrinogenicity. Pregnancy and the neonate. In a review1 of antituberculous treatment in pregnant patients it was reported that over 95% of 1480 pregnancies in which isoniazid had been given resulted in a normal term infant. Slightly more than 1% of the infants/fetus- es were abnormal and many of these abnormalities were CNS related. Isoniazid is therefore recognised as being suitable for use in regimens for the treatment of tuberculosis in pregnant pa- tients.2,3 Pyridoxine supplementation is recommended2 (see Treatment of Adverse Effects, above). Preventive therapy with isoniazid is generally delayed until after delivery unless other risk factors are present. 1. Snider DE, et al. Treatment of tuberculosis during pregnancy.
